newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk sale deal signed Friday.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk sale deal signed Friday.

text.p: A controversial agreement by which a unit of Russia's powerful Uneximbank bought 38 percent of Russia's biggest metals company Norilsk Nickel was signed on Friday, a bank spokesman said on Monday.

ZAO Svift, part of the Interrosprom industrial group which in turn is part of the Uneximbank group, won the stake which amounts to 51 percent of voting shares and was previously controlled by Uneximbank under the shares-for-loans programme, with a bid of about $250 million, Uneximbank spokesman Sergei Chernitsyn told Reuters.
"Yes, the sale was signed on Friday evening," he said.

Under the terms of the agreement, the winner of the tender must also invest at least $300 million in RAO Norilsky Nikel. Chernitsyn said these investment funds must be transferred within five days of the agreement being signed.

It was unclear until the last moment whether the tender would be allowed to proceed last Tuesday. Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin had called for it to be halted, but at the last minute allowed it to go ahead.
However Chernomyrdin had instigated an investigation into whether the tender was conducted legally.
But the State Property Fund, the Federal Property Committee and the General Prosecutor agreed late last week that the tender had been legally carried out, Russian news agencies reported on Monday.
Norilsk is one of the world's top suppliers of platinum group metals and nickel.
